answer: Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 113 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the juniper ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the timber review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. A near-duplicate is rejected at the bridge gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. That is 11 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
